newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-CAMBRIDGE COMPLETE VARSITY HAT-TRICK.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CAMBRIDGE COMPLETE VARSITY HAT-TRICK.

text.p: Cambridge University claimed the Bowring Bowl for the third successive year at Twickenham on Tuesday by beating Oxford University 23-7 in a lacklustre 115th Varsity Match.
Oxford were given early encouragement by their Australian centre Trevor Walsh who charged down a kick and raced 50 metres to score under the posts after just four minutes.

But it was to prove their only moment of attacking success in front of 72,000 spectators and Cambridge ran out comfortable winners with the aid of two tries and a drop-goal from centre Matthew Singer and 10 points from the boot of New Zealander Paul Surridge.
A minute's silence was observed before kick-off for Ian Tucker, the Australian student who died following a match between Oxford and Saracens in October.

In the circumstances, there was concern when South African Quentin de Bruyn, Oxford's captain, was knocked unconscious and had to be carried off in the second-half. He recovered sufficiently to watch the rest of the game from the stands.
